name: Grand Cabin Hotel Naha Oroku
detail: It's like a hybrid between a capsule hotel and a business hotel. The bed was in a spacious room, so I was able to sleep well. There were plenty of amenities and rentals like hair irons, making it comfortable to stay. The free drink service and meals were convenient; even at late hours, I could purchase frozen food and cup noodles, and with a microwave available, I didn’t have any meal issues. It's just one station from the airport, making it perfect for late arrivals and early departures. However, for those who want to sleep in the next morning, it's hard to say. Everyone starts getting ready before 5 AM for early morning flights, so the sounds of footsteps, doors, and preparations can be bothersome and wake you up. Earplugs are a must!! That way, you might be able to sleep better. Overall, for the price, it was a hotel with good facilities that I would like to use again.

name: The Kitchen Hostel Ao
detail: I used the service for the first time, and the staff's explanations were thorough, making my stay comfortable. There were plenty of restrooms and showers, so I didn't have to wait to use them, which was great. The shared space was very comfortable, and there was a convenience store nearby, so I had no issues. Despite being reasonably priced, the amenities were well-stocked, leading to a high level of satisfaction.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Hotel Abest Naha Kokusai Street
detail: The overall accommodation experience was very satisfactory, with a convenient location, easy transportation, and nearby activities being quite accessible. The room cleaning was well done, the facilities and services were complete, the WiFi worked smoothly, and the staff was enthusiastic and attentive. Overall, the lodging experience was comfortable, with excellent value for money, making it a highly recommended choice.

name: Green Rich Hotel & Capsule Naha Artificial hot spring Futamata Yunohana
detail: I used a room for my one-night stay in Naha. It is not the typical capsule hotel with a large section, but instead has properly locked rooms. While capsule hotels are affordable, they come with a bit of tension from shared living; however, with a room, that concern is gone. Since it is located in the entertainment district of Matsuyama, I was a bit worried about the safety at night, but being slightly away from the center means it is quiet at night. Having a FamilyMart right in front is also convenient. It is positioned almost exactly midway between Miebashi Station and Kenchomae Station on the Yui Rail, but if walking, Miebashi Station feels closer. Breakfast costs 1,400 yen (1,500 yen on the day). It is a buffet style, offering Okinawan local dishes and side dishes. The variety is somewhat limited, but considering the price, it is just right for a morning meal. Having a large public bath is definitely a plus. It helps wash away the fatigue of the day, allowing for a good night's sleep.

name: APA HOTEL NAHAMATSUYAMA
detail: The environment was comfortable with clean bedding. The breakfast was delicious and typical of Okinawa, featuring taco rice, tacos, and Okinawa soba (of course, there was also ap curry), and I was able to take coffee back to my room and relax.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Y's Cabin & Hotel Naha
detail: If you only need a place to sleep, it's a clean and very cost-effective accommodation. You can't store things like suitcases, but the front desk lends out chains. The large public bath was spacious and clean. I didn't particularly mind the noise from those around me. On the first floor, there's a simple drink bar and a place to eat food you bring in. It's located just one block back from Kokusai Street, making it quiet.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Santiago Guesthouse Naha
detail: There were clean linens and bedding without stains, a nice shower, and even towels were provided, so I had no issues at all. If I had to nitpick, the only downside was that there were only stairs to get to the guest rooms, which was a bit of a hassle. The location was good, and it turned out to be a wonderful trip. Thank you very much.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Guest House My Place
detail: The dormitory room is small, but there are proper storage spaces and lockers for each person, which is sufficient. There is a power outlet by the bedside, and it was quiet at night, allowing for a good sleep. I didn't use the bathroom in the room, but the bathroom in the shared space was comfortable. The location is a bit far, but there is parking available, and a convenience store nearby. I think this low price is good if you just need a place to sleep.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Daiwa Roynet Hotel Naha Kokusai-dori
detail: Directly connected to the station, close to Kokusai-dori, and there are plenty of convenience stores and restaurants nearby. There is a roof from the station to the hotel, so it’s fine even in light rain! The room was clean and easy to use. This was a hotel I would like to use again. There was also self-baggage service after check-out, so I could store my luggage from morning until heading to the airport in the evening, making it very convenient! Being directly connected to the station is great!
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Prince Smart Inn Naha
detail: It's a recently established place, very clean, and the facilities are new. The staff are friendly, and they provide a simple breakfast of bagel sandwiches and coffee in the morning. There's a Family Mart right next door, and a Seven-Eleven across the street. It's a leisurely 10-15 minute walk to Kokusai Street and just 5 minutes to Yuirail. There's also a bus stop just 2-3 minutes away from the accommodation, making it convenient for those on foot.
